headline: First review since Aug 18. Portfolio value ~Rs 10.32M, P/L +Rs 276K (+2.75% on cost) — down from +3.4% a week ago, almost entirely AVN's further slide (Rs 32.97 → Rs 31.27, now −30.6% on cost). KSE-100 chopped through a volatile week on US-Iran/oil headlines and closed today at 176,967 (−0.11%), pushing the drawdown from the Jan ATH to ~6.6% (from ~5.6% last review) — still below the 10% deploy line. Biggest news: Fatima Fertilizer's H1 results beat (profit +20.7% YoY) but the company skipped its interim dividend. AVN is being escalated from TRIM to a full EXIT call — the sell-half plan has now sat unexecuted for over three weeks while the price fell straight through its Rs 34–38 target zone, and Sep 2 earnings (8 days out) is too close to keep waiting.
market: Choppy week: KSE-100 swung between +600 and −2,547 point sessions on shifting US-Iran/Strait-of-Hormuz headlines and oil-price moves, closing today (Mon Aug 24/25) at 176,966.69, down 199.84 pts (−0.11%) after giving back an intraday high near 178,123. Week-on-week the index was down ~1.6%. Drawdown from the Jan 23 ATH (189,556) is now ~6.6%, up from ~5.6% at the last review — trending toward, but still well short of, the 10% line that would justify deploying the AICF/MICF cash reserve. Backdrop stayed constructive: SBP held its policy rate at 11.5% (no new MPC meeting since the Jul 27 pause), the State Bank confirmed receipt of $1.3B under the IMF's EFF/RSF programmes, and July's current account deficit narrowed sharply (-38% YoY, -60% MoM) to $328M. EARNINGS/DIVIDENDS — Fatima Fertilizer's H1 2026 results landed Aug 21: consolidated profit Rs 20.44B (+20.7% YoY), EPS Rs 9.73 (vs Rs 8.06) on revenue +12.7% to Rs 130.61B — a clear beat — but the board skipped the interim dividend, citing an uncertain operating environment, geopolitical risk and continued GIDC ambiguity; management explicitly said this isn't a change to long-term dividend policy. Meezan Bank's H1 numbers (already known) showed consolidated profit +3% YoY to Rs 48.64B on the Rs 8/share dividend already paid; new since last review is a Shariah-compliant credit-card launch (2027 rollout) and branch count at 1,150, targeting 1,250 by year-end. FABL's Rs 1.50/share interim (approved Aug 6) still has no published ex-date after repeated checks. AVN — no new company news since Aug 17's $6.3mn order; the stock kept falling (Rs 33.20 → 32.97 → 31.27 over three reviews) with zero signs of the 'recovery' the Sep 2 exit-deadline was conditioned on. EFERT — nothing new since the early-Aug briefings; still on WATCH into Q3. Fund NAVs (funds_updated: Aug 13) are now stale for 12 days — the MUFAP scraper issue flagged Aug 13 is unresolved.

actions.title: Avanceon — escalating TRIM to full EXIT: unexecuted for 3+ weeks, price now below the entire sell zone, earnings in 8 days
actions.detail: Your worst performer, now −30.6% (Rs 31.27, down from Rs 32.97 last review and Rs 33.20 three weeks ago). The 'sell half at Monday Aug 3's open' plan is now over three weeks overdue with the full 24,500 shares still showing in holdings — and the price has fallen straight through the Rs 34–38 zone it was supposed to be sold into, so a half-measure at this point locks in a worse exit than doing nothing would have. No new company news since Aug 17's $6.3mn fuel-retail order, which doesn't touch the underlying problem (FY25 net income −68%, margins 12%→4%, three-year shareholder return −32%). Sep 2, 2026 earnings — 8 days away — was set as the hard deadline for a full exit 'if no recovery by then'; there has been no recovery, only further decline, over the three weeks since that deadline was set. Waiting for the earnings print itself now adds pure event risk on a name whose fundamentals are already broken, for no offsetting upside case. This is an exception to the general accumulate-and-hold stance — AVN's call has been fundamentals-driven since Jul 2026, not a valuation call. Recommend selling the entire position at market now rather than holding through the earnings date.
actions.target: Sell all 24,500 shares at market (~Rs 31) — split proceeds ~55% into MEBL (~Rs 421K), ~45% into MZNPETF (~Rs 345K)

actions.title: Meezan Bank — core compounder, all dividends processed
actions.detail: +57.2% (Rs 571.83), Pakistan's premier Islamic bank with a structural deposit advantage — exactly the 20-year holding you want. H1 consolidated profit +3% YoY to Rs 48.64B on the Rs 8.00/share interim already paid (ex-date Aug 18, done, no more reminders). New since last review: management confirmed two Shariah-compliant card products (Meezan Charge Card, Islamic Financing Card) launching commercially in 2027, and branch count at 1,150 with 100 more planned by year-end — steady expansion, not a catalyst. Still well above the Rs 500 add line; add on any 10%+ dip. This is also the primary destination for AVN exit proceeds this review.

actions.title: Fatima Fertilizer — H1 results beat (profit +20.7%), but skipped the interim dividend
actions.detail: +46.3% (Rs 157.25, down slightly since last review despite the earnings beat — the dividend skip likely weighed more than the profit growth did). H1 2026 results out Aug 21: consolidated profit Rs 20.44B (+20.7% YoY), EPS Rs 9.73 vs Rs 8.06, revenue +12.7% to Rs 130.61B — genuinely strong underlying performance and concessionary-gas cost advantage still intact. But the board chose not to declare an interim dividend, citing an uncertain operating environment, geopolitical risk, and unresolved GIDC exposure; management was explicit this isn't a policy change. Earnings thesis confirmed, moving off WATCH back to HOLD, but worth checking the next dividend announcement to see if the skip was a one-off or the start of a pattern.
